The chain's 2026-08-30 heat names one money-corner link (emissions-aftertreatment-and-catalyst) and four UNDISCOVERED-verdict links (federal-minor-nsr-rule, state-air-permitting-authority, air-permitting-and-dispersion-modeling, emissions-aftertreatment-and-catalyst), which is this run's DEPTH-scope set (3 distinct links since the money-corner link is also UNDISCOVERED). air-permitting-and-dispersion-modeling closes TARGET_MET with 5 distinct listed issuers (Tetra Tech, AECOM, Jacobs Solutions, Onterris/ONT, ICF International), reusing three issuers' identity evidence verbatim from data/mappings/data-center-moratoria.json (same legal issuers, same-issuer reuse rule) and establishing two fresh (ONT, ICF International) with dated SEC EDGAR identity_evidence and fresh role evidence specific to Clean Air Act minor-NSR air permitting and dispersion modeling, not the land-use/water permitting role those three issuers already hold on data-center-moratoria. emissions-aftertreatment-and-catalyst closes EXHAUSTED at 4 of the 5-issuer DEPTH target (Caterpillar, Cummins, Fuel Tech, CECO Environmental), with a full multi-source record: a 25-hit SEC EDGAR full text search finding only power-generation utilities beyond the already-counted Cummins, plus direct confirmation that the leading named private specialist (EcoCAT) is not public; Johnson Matthey plc (LSE:JMAT, owner of Cormetech, the chain's named global SCR catalyst leader) is a known public issuer whose identity could not be established from a fetchable official London Stock Exchange or FCA National Storage Mechanism source this session (JS-rendered pages, one HTTP 403) and is carried as a directional finding rather than a fifth counted issuer. federal-minor-nsr-rule and state-air-permitting-authority each close EXHAUSTED at 0 issuers with a full two-domain, two-source-type record (epa.gov official plus parrbrown.com industry legal commentary for the federal rule; townhall.virginia.gov official plus hunton.com industry legal commentary for the representative state authority), each with zero-hit control_probe records, confirming these are purely governmental functions with no possible commercial issuer, exactly as the chain's own map_limitation already stated. Every other link (the 10 out-of-scope links) carries at least one ACTIVE placement with dated issuer-role evidence (onsite-reciprocating-gensets: Caterpillar; packaged-gas-turbines: Baker Hughes; fuel-cell-permit-avoidance: Bloom Energy; gas-supply-and-interconnection: Energy Transfer, Williams; emissions-monitoring-and-compliance: ONT; bridge-power-rental-fleets: United Rentals; behind-the-meter-power-developers: Williams; data-center-developer-demand: Oracle, reusing its identity evidence verbatim from data/mappings/ai-infrastructure.json) or a recorded search explaining why zero placements is correct: liquid-fuel-logistics-and-storage is MOSTLY_PRIVATE by the chain's own design (Mansfield Energy and the other named fuel haulers are private) and power-equipment-shared is a declared duplicate of ai-infrastructure/power-equipment per BLK-04, so no placement is created here to avoid double-counting; its seven tickers are counted only in that mapping. Most role evidence was reused directly from this chain's own already-fetched, already-cited evidence (Caterpillar, Baker Hughes, Bloom Energy, Energy Transfer, Williams x2, ONT, United Rentals, Oracle all cite sources the chain-build run already verified) rather than re-fetched, since the chain and its prior mapping are both in this run's required reading. 15 distinct issuers across 18 placements (11 newly established with fresh SEC EDGAR identity_evidence, 4 reused verbatim for the same legal issuer from other mappings). target_issuers_per_link is 5 per DEPTH mode. No issuer, listing, placement, or search was invented; every number and every ticker traces to a fetched, dated source, and the one shortfall (Johnson Matthey) is stated as a tooling gap rather than papered over. Mapping left ACTIVE per method 6A; the author never marks its own work COMPLETE.

Placement-audit follow-up amendment (Ron, 2026-09-04, 'everything now'): the 2026-09-04 fresh-context placement audits (commit f187057) PASSED CATERPILLAR, CUMMINS, FUEL-TECH and CECO-ENVIRONMENTAL on emissions-aftertreatment-and-catalyst with live-fetched verbatim excerpts, but every role-evidence item on those four placements still carried tag INFERRED, which check_screen.py refuses on an un-audited mapping (a screen row needs all-VERIFIED evidence). Re-fetched, live, every role-evidence URL on these seven placements (the four above plus TETRA-TECH, AECOM, JACOBS-SOLUTIONS on air-permitting-and-dispersion-modeling) this run, from a LOCAL session with curl/WebFetch access, and checked each excerpt verbatim against the fetched page text. TETRA-TECH's existing evidence item, on a link with no placement_audits entries, already cited the issuer's own official page and, once re-fetched, verbatim supported the full claim: retagged INFERRED->VERIFIED in place with a fuller, still-verbatim excerpt, so this placement is now all-VERIFIED. For the four audited emissions-aftertreatment-and-catalyst placements (CATERPILLAR, CUMMINS, FUEL-TECH, CECO-ENVIRONMENTAL), the sampled evidence[0] item was left untouched in every case, even where re-fetching CECO-ENVIRONMENTAL's own cited page confirmed its claim verbatim, because rewriting a placement_audits[]-sampled item changes placement_claim_digest and would silently invalidate that entry's PASS status without a re-audit (check_map.py caught exactly this on a first attempt at this amendment, which is reverted); a fresh-context run universe-audit --placement is the correct path to re-sample and revalidate those four items, not an author-run edit. Instead, for CATERPILLAR and CUMMINS the existing item cites a third-party compliance guide (powergenenterprises.com, secondary), so a new VERIFIED item was appended from each issuer's own official Tier-4/aftertreatment page confirming the narrower claim it actually supports verbatim. For FUEL-TECH the existing item cites a Motley Fool earnings-call transcript mirror (secondary), so a new VERIFIED item was appended from Fuel Tech's own case-study page confirming the 20-SCR/data-center-turbine claim verbatim. For CECO-ENVIRONMENTAL the existing item already cites CECO's own page, and a new VERIFIED item was appended from the same URL with the full verbatim sentence in place of the original's thin excerpt. AECOM and JACOBS-SOLUTIONS's existing items (air-permitting link, no placement_audits entries) already cite the issuer's own official page, but on live re-fetch the page did not verbatim support the data-center/tall-stack/New-Source-Review specifics in the original claim, so those items stay INFERRED as written; appended a new VERIFIED item on each stating the narrower claim the same official page does support. Net effect: TETRA-TECH is now the only one of the seven placements with all evidence VERIFIED (screen-admissible under audit_scope PLACEMENT without a further audit); the other six each gained one new VERIFIED item but retain one INFERRED item (secondary source, or an audited item left untouched, or a claim that overreaches its own primary source), so none of the six is yet all-VERIFIED. No issuer, listing, placement, or prior evidence row was deleted or altered beyond the one TETRA-TECH retag and the six appended items named above; every added item is a live fetch dated 2026-09-04. Every listing's identity_evidence for these seven issuers was already VERIFIED (SEC EDGAR submissions, from the 2026-09-04 author run) and untouched here. Mapping left ACTIVE; this session performs no audit, writes no placement_audits entry, and marks no link or the mapping COMPLETE.
